purpose: Finite functional-form and covariance sensitivity analyses; preserve historical estimates and source data.

country_strict_N20.cohort: existing strict N20 linear-model cases and identical retained analysis frame per country
country_strict_N20.temperature: existing ERA5 tmean; identical existing exposure assignment
country_strict_N20.model: matched conditional Poisson/log-link, original country-specific calendar design plus state and calendar-date fixed effects; only temperature basis changes between linear and spline fits
country_strict_N20.inference: two-way cluster-robust covariance by state and calendar date, with intersection term retained; report retained state/date/intersection cluster counts; t reference df=min(G_state-1,G_date-1)

spline.basis: explicit linear temperature column plus two nonlinear natural-cubic columns
spline.knots: one common exposure knot set per country, calculated without outcome data from pooled lag-0..7 temperatures in the matched complete-case analysis frame: boundary knots P5/P95, interior knots P33.333/P66.667
spline.all_lag_basis: apply identical fixed country-specific basis to each of lags 0..7
spline.nonlinear_test: nested Wald F test of the 16 added nonlinear coefficients (2 per lag × 8 lags) equal to zero, compared with the matched lag-specific linear model; do not test all 24 spline coefficients equal to zero
spline.contrasts: P10, P50, P90, P95 Celsius versus P50, applying the contrast jointly to all eight lag coefficients
spline.curve: 100 equally spaced Celsius values from exposure P5 to P95, pointwise RR and 95% CI versus P50

reports: all coefficients and full coefficient covariance
analysis sample flow and retained G
cluster-robust covariance eigenvalue/PSD diagnostics including min eigenvalue and relative negative eigenvalue scale

brazil_2008_2022_region_primary.frame: existing regional primary frame, 2008-2022; retain original outcome, complete-case rules, fixed effects, calendar terms, humidity and other covariates, and fire0-7 specification
brazil_2008_2022_region_primary.temperature_sensitivity: replace only the original linear temperature lag0-7 terms with the same 3df natural-cubic basis and fixed knot/contrast/curve rules as above, knots/percentiles estimated from the matched primary analysis frame without outcome data
brazil_2008_2022_region_primary.nonlinear_test: nested Wald F test of the 16 added nonlinear temperature coefficients conditional on unchanged fire0-7 and other original covariates, versus matched linear temperature+fire model
brazil_2008_2022_region_primary.inference: two-way cluster-robust covariance by hrid and calendar date (including intersection term); t df=min(G_hrid-1,G_date-1)
outputs: sample flow and retained cluster counts
temperature curve and P10/P50/P90/P95 contrasts vs P50 with pointwise 95% CI

brazil_2008_2022_historical_inference.temperature_fire: refit/reconstruct the unchanged historical linear temperature+fire lag0-7 specification on its original matched frame; update inference only to two-way cluster-robust hrid+date covariance
brazil_2008_2022_historical_inference.same_day_compound: retain original same-day compound-category model and point estimates; recompute hrid+date two-way cluster covariance and interval/p-values
brazil_2008_2022_historical_inference.historical: do not overwrite or edit any previous estimate or output; label old and updated inference distinctly

uncertainty: use two-sided 95% intervals with t critical values using df=min(retained cluster counts)-1; report estimates, SEs, intervals and p values
eigen: eigendecompose symmetrized covariance; record min/max eigenvalues, count of negative eigenvalues, and abs(min eigenvalue)/max(abs eigenvalue); do not silently project to PSD
exclusions: no new countries, diagnoses, manuscript edits, DOCX operations, or additional analyses
